status: 여름철새 10만 마리 이상 · 나그네새 수천 마리

months.note: 4월 말에 오기 시작해 10월에 떠나며, 5월 중순~7월에 둥지를 틀고 새끼를 기른다.

summary: 습지 가장자리의 갈대와 풀숲에 사는 여름철새로, 전국에 산다. 갈대나 부들 줄기를 서로 엮어 둥지를 만든다. 주로 갈대나 풀 속에서 지내다가 울 때는 갈대 끝에 올라 큰 소리로 우는데, 한곳에 여러 마리가 있기도 해서 한창 울 때는 수컷들의 소리가 많이 들린다. 국외에서는 러시아 연해주, 중국 동남부, 일본, 동남아시아에 분포한다.
young: 어른새와 비슷하나 위쪽이 더 붉은 기를 띠고, 아랫면 전체가 더 짙은 황갈색이며 멱과 윗가슴에 가는 세로줄이 없다.

similar.how: 큰부리개개비는 뚜렷한 눈썹선이 없어 얼굴이 밋밋하고, 부리가 더 짧고 두툼하다.

art.subject: Oriental Reed Warbler (Acrocephalus orientalis), adult in summer (sexes alike): upperparts plain warm olive-brown with no streaks; a prominent whitish-buff supercilium, strongest in front of and just behind the eye; a dark eye-stripe; whitish throat; faint fine greyish streaks on the lower throat and upper breast; breast sides and flanks washed buff; belly whitish; wings and tail plain brown; long, stout bill with a dark upper mandible and a pinkish-yellow lower mandible; orange-red mouth lining when singing; dark eye; bluish-grey legs.
art.pose: singing loudly from the top of a reed stem, bill open
art.scene: Korean summer reedbed at the edge of a marsh; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view clinging to a vertical reed stem: plain olive-brown upperparts, whitish-buff supercilium, dark eye-stripe, buff-washed flanks, whitish belly, long stout bill, long rounded tail, bluish-grey legs
adult singing from the top of a reed, side view: bill wide open showing the orange-red mouth, whitish throat with faint grey streaks, smooth crown with no crest, whitish belly, long rounded tail
art.build: Large reed warbler, clearly longer than a sparrow but slim, with a long tail. No crest; the crown feathers lie flat, the forehead sloping into a slightly peaked crown. Bill long and strong, nearly as long as the head, straight and pointed. Legs strong, bluish-grey, gripping vertical reed stems. Wings fairly short; at rest the wingtips reach the base of the tail. Tail long and rounded. Sings loudly from reed tops with the bill wide open and the head tilted up.
avoid: Do not paint dark streaks on the back or crown; the upperparts are plain.
Do not paint a black stripe above the white supercilium; that is the much smaller Black-browed Reed Warbler.
Do not paint yellow or green tones; the bird is brown and buff.
Do not paint a short, fine bill; the bill is long and strong.
